reason: The repair cell needs the copied instructions and amino acids to make collagen support.
expectation: The cell will use the instructions and amino acids to begin making collagen.

effect: The repair cell has made collagen chains from amino acids using the RNA instructions. The chains still need processing and export.
reaction: The picture makes the ribosome’s role clear, and I’m curious how the chains reach the wound.
reason: The processing and export membranes appear suited to preparing the new collagen chains for delivery outside the cell.
expectation: The membranes will process and package the collagen for export.

effect: The repair cell processed and exported collagen, forming supporting fibers outside the cell. Those fibers can now replace material beneath the scrape.
reaction: The three panels clarify how material made inside a cell becomes support outside it; I had missed that the cell was the required hotspot.
reason: The new supporting fibers appear suited to filling the missing support beneath the scrape.
expectation: The fibers will restore supporting material beneath the damaged surface.

effect: The new collagen fibers span the deeper gaps, but the surface cells have not yet closed the scrape.
reaction: The cross-section makes the distinction between replacing support and closing the surface clear.
reason: The cells at the scrape’s edge are positioned to close the remaining surface gap.

choice.combine: Skin cells at the scrape’s edge

expectation: The edge cells will help renew the protective surface over the repaired support.

effect: The edge cells first need local repair signals; they are now dividing and spreading toward the gap.
reaction: I had expected to place the cells directly, so the signaling step was a useful surprise.
reason: The spreading surface cells can now help close the remaining gap in the rebuilding body.
expectation: The cells will cover the gap and renew the protective surface.

effect: The surface gap is closed, while the deeper collagen is still remodeling and may leave a scar.
reaction: The distinction between a closed surface and continuing deeper repair was satisfying and clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making and exporting collagen was most worthwhile: the result connected work inside the repair cell to support outside it.

leastWorthwhile.text: The requirement to use the repair cell as a hotspot for processing was initially unclear, although the compatibility feedback resolved it.

surprise.text: I expected the edge cells to go directly onto the wound; the local signals first prompted them to divide and spread.

arbitrary.text: Using the repair cell as the hotspot felt slightly arbitrary at first because the collagen chains and processing membranes seemed like a plausible pair. The resulting panels explained what happened inside the cell.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter. The progression from making collagen to closing the surface made the biology understandable, and I would be curious to see another connected process.
